newsitem.title: UK: UK commercial radio wins record advertising share.
newsitem.headline: UK commercial radio wins record advertising share.

text.p: Britain's commercial radio stations claimed a record 4.9 percent of the country's total advertising market in the July to September 1996 quarter, a trade group reported on Monday.
Commercial radio's previous greatest share of the UK advertising market had been in July to September 1995, when it claimed 4.7 percent, the Radio Advertising Bureau said.
The total advertising market includes radio, television, press and posters.

Radio advertising revenues rose 15.5 percent to 300.1 million pounds in the July to September 1996 quarter, outstripping the 5.7 percent growth rate for the total advertising market during the same period, the Radio Advertising Bureau said. The Advertising Bureau cited figures compiled by the UK Advertising Association.
Radio's share of the moving annual total now stands at a 4.6 percent.

"Commercial radio has been the medium of the 1990s with advertising revenue having more than doubled since the beginning of the decade," Justin Sampson, director of operations at the Advertising Bureau, said. "We are confident that by the year 2000 the medium, through further growth, will account for well over five percent of display advertising."
